subject: Agriculture
title: CRISPR in Crops
description: Learn CRISPR in Crops in one minute.

hook.text: CRISPR can edit a plant's own genes without inserting foreign DNA. It's faster, cheaper, and avoids the GMO label.

buildup.text: Traditional breeding takes 10–15 years to develop a new crop variety. CRISPR can achieve the same result in 1–2 years.

discovery.text: CRISPR-edited tomatoes with boosted GABA—a nutrient that lowers blood pressure—are already sold in Japan.

twist.text: The US and Japan regulate CRISPR-edited crops like conventional breeds. The EU regulates them like GMOs. Rules diverge wildly.

climax.text: CRISPR could create climate-resilient, disease-resistant, nutritious crops rapidly—if regulation keeps pace with science.

punchline.text: Edit one gene, save a crop. CRISPR is breeding on fast-forward.

quiz.question: How does CRISPR differ from traditional GMOs?
options: CRISPR edits a plant's own genes without inserting foreign DNA
